data.title: Plugin
data.tagline: A distributable software package installed into a host application to provide extended capabilities, commands, or UI via standardized extension points.
data.learningOutcome: You can choose between a Plugin, Skill, and Hook and know that a plugin cannot guarantee correct generated code.
data.description: For example, an editor plugin can add a sidebar, shortcuts, code completion, or diff previews. Other plugins may only add commands or service integrations. A plugin does not require a UI, and it is not the same as a Skill task method or a Hook event script.

learning.assumes: You have used a code editor and seen a sidebar or code-completion extension.
learning.outcome: You can choose between a Plugin, Skill, and Hook and know that a plugin cannot guarantee correct generated code.

distinctions.label: Agent Skill
distinctions.explanation: A Plugin packages code to extend the host application's UI, commands, or runtime; a Skill instructs an AI agent with domain workflows, scripts, and guidelines.

explanation.title: Provide an editor entry point
explanation.text: A plugin can add a sidebar, shortcuts, inline suggestions, or a configuration panel.

explanation.title: Collect current context
explanation.text: After a selection, it can send file and language context to the model and show the result in the editor.

explanation.title: Make changes reviewable
explanation.text: A side-by-side diff lets the user compare a proposal before accepting it into the file.

data.boundary: A Plugin is installable software, a Skill is a reusable task method, and a Hook is an event-triggered background command. A plugin improves integration but cannot guarantee bug-free output.

lessonPractice.title: A team needs an editor sidebar and diff preview. Which extension fits?

options.label: Use a Plugin to package the UI entry point and editor integration
options.feedback: Correct. Plugins can provide sidebars, shortcuts, inline suggestions, and diff views in an editor.

options.label: Use a Skill because Skills automatically provide visual UI across editors
options.feedback: A Skill mainly provides a reusable task method and files; it is not an editor UI extension.

options.label: Use a Hook because a background event script will create the full sidebar
options.feedback: A Hook listens for events and runs preset tasks; it does not provide a sidebar or diff interface.

data.agentPrompt: First classify this need as editor integration, a reusable task workflow, or an event-triggered check. Design a Plugin only if it needs a sidebar, shortcuts, or a diff preview.
